note: EMPTY, and that is a statement about the 11 guards in tools/dev/anti-vacuity-cases.json. Swept 2026-08-30 over the whole population. 177 test files scan the tree; 164 also state a zero-verdict (146 under the census's spellings, plus 18 that used a spelling the census did not recognise until this sweep widened it). 89 remain once guards whose only corpus is a directory they created themselves are removed. FOUR lenses, each answering something the one before it could not. (1) Blank the bound corpus root. (2) Blank that root's test files too — a guard whose corpus IS test files sees an untouched tree under lens 1. (3) Blank EVERY root at once so no inferred binding can explain a pass, and record how much SURVIVED: a green over a tree the guard's own imports refilled is the instrument having no verdict, not the guard having none. (4) Judge a TEST, not a file, by comparing `expect()` counts between the blanked and intact arms. THREE real findings, all fixed with a paired control: `no-leftover-backup-files` floored the tracked list but not the `existsSync` narrowing; `cross-slice-cycle` had TWO loop-body bans over `readdir`, and an empty listing ran them zero times; `manifest-codex-compat` floored the directory listing while its work sat behind a `catch { continue }`, asserting 67 times over the real corpus and ONCE over the blanked one, green both ways. The rest of the 89: 67 red, 13 that throw when their corpus is absent, 9 green that are all instrument limits — 6 refilled by their own import closure, 1 whose corpus is the git index, 1 whose corpus is the host filesystem (`/sbin`), 1 whose corpus is `.github/workflows`, since made a corpus root and proven non-vacuous by blanking that directory directly. KNOWN LIMITS, stated rather than papered. Lens 4 counts assertions, so it is blind to an AGGREGATE verdict — `expect(offenders).toEqual([])` costs one call whether the scan read 3,000 files or none. That case is covered by lens 3 at FILE level: measured, 45 of the 48 files holding such a test go red or throw on a blanked tree, so the corpus loss is caught somewhere in the file even when the individual test would pass, and the 3 exceptions are the adjudicated greens above. Conversely lens 3 is blind to a vacuous test inside a file that is red for another reason, which is how `cross-slice-cycle` survived it. Neither lens subsumes the other, and neither subsumes the static census: the census is what demands a floor from a NEW guard. Re-running the full sweep is on demand, not on every commit — it builds two mirrors per file and spawns a run per test: `bun run tools/dev/per-test-vacuity.ts <cases.json>`, where cases.json is `[{"file": "…"}, …]`. This CORRECTS an earlier note reporting '16 more vacuous guards' from an interrupted partial sweep: every one was a lens artifact. A single blanked root cannot tell 'the guard noticed nothing' from 'the root it actually reads was left standing'.
